title: A proposed role requires exclusion from incompatible slots

basis.proposal_quote: A concrete role imposes a semantic incompatibility boundary, so an item-like whole cannot freely occupy a process-only slot (and conversely).

predecessor_audit.result: Target-masked neighboring-role comparison; zero policy winners and zero confirmed lexemes. It supplies structural edge compatibility, not independently semantic incompatible slots.
Context profiles produced leads but zero new role selections; inherited tags are explicitly not independent semantics or renderer licenses.
Role candidates remain replaceable and context-bound; specific medium identity is unresolved.

logical_finding: The proposal has a possible falsifier shape but does not yet operationalize a concrete meaning question. It names generic roles and structural slots, but fixes neither one target whole nor an independently semantic compatible/incompatible contrast. A structural/null separation can show that a candidate is absent from a tagged slot; it cannot by itself show that the role is semantically impossible there. Matching section, position, frequency and neighboring frame controls remove some confounds, but do not validate the semantic interpretation of the slot labels.
countermodel: A compact notation may reuse one whole as a quantity-bearing item in an ordinary process frame, or omit the process operator while retaining the item. The same structural slot can therefore be tagged process-only by the analyst while remaining semantically compatible with the candidate role. Under this model, repeated held-folio occupancy is a failure of the proposed slot interpretation or a context-polymorphic role, not a logical refutation of the whole's quantity/item meaning. Conversely, a low rate can reflect page/position convention without confirming the meaning.
smallest_decisive_question: For one selected whole W and one fixed role R, can an independently anchored semantic slot contract establish that slot S is incompatible with R before inspecting W's outcomes? Then, on held occurrences, does W occupy S repeatedly enough to cross a preregistered bound, while matched opaque controls do not? Decision rule: validated repeated occupancy falsifies R; validated exclusion supports a necessary-condition check only; if S is only a structural tag, record a null/compatibility result and make no semantic decision.
successor_and_route_check: The route check returns GDT762 and related role/context screens, but no exact successor that supplies the missing semantic slot anchor. They should not be treated as IDEA000005's pass/fail. No global failure follows and no new data is automatically required; first establish whether the existing cached panel contains a predeclared, independently grounded S.
decision: Do not authorize IDEA000005 as a semantic falsifier in its current generic form. Retain it as a proposal for a narrowly scoped necessary-condition question after fixing W, R, S, held occurrences, bound and semantic anchoring rule.
